## Problem

The launcher arms its 50-minute child bound when it spawns the child (`src/host/hosted-runtime.ts:319-326`, timer at `src/replay/runtime.ts:290-296`), but the child measures its own run budget from a later instant: `deadline: clock.now() + RUN_DEADLINE_MS` is evaluated at `src/host/actions.ts:273`, after the source clone and refresh, review-client setup and Codex preflight at `src/host/actions.ts:154-244`. Each git operation may take up to 120 s and each preflight operation 20 s, so the real drain cushion before SIGTERM is `5 min - setup` rather than the five minutes the constant ordering documents. On a slow setup the launcher can still kill the child during the mandatory review drain, the CI approval or the result log.

The raised P1 is closed for realistic runs: sessions settle by start + 20 min + 30 s inside the 40-minute loop window, so parking a durable implementation intent needs an implausible ~14.5-minute setup.

## Acceptance

- Anchor the child deadline to an instant captured before the setup phase, or reduce the constant to cover the setup offset, so the documented five-minute drain cushion is a true invariant.
- Bind the invariant in a test that measures from the same origin as the launcher rather than only comparing the two constants.

Severity: P2, non-blocking.

## Acceptance

An unverified publication observation is preserved as unresolved and retried, so a recovered read of the legitimate predecessor head cannot be treated as an unrelated head.

Problem

A completed current-head review with only unresolved P2/P3 findings takes the correction path. `rejectedReceipt` treats every unresolved severity as rejection (`src/repair/loop.ts:2351-2353`), and `unresolvedSeverities.length > 0` selects `advanceToCorrection` (`:4900`, `:4951-4955`). The trusted merge gate blocks unresolved P0/P1 (`src/repair/review-gate.ts:134-148`), so the ordinary repair loop spends further correction attempts on findings that the merge policy permits.

The deterministic maintenance consumer now makes `work`/`blocked` records delivery-eligible after all three review rounds are spent (`ops/hosted-autonomy.ts:74-92`). That mitigates the previously claimed permanent hosted-delivery blockage; this issue is limited to the remaining unnecessary correction work in the repair loop.

## Acceptance

A completed P2/P3-only review follows the documented non-blocking delivery path without consuming a correction attempt. Unresolved P0/P1 findings, task-acceptance checks, exact-head review, CI and merge gates stay enforced.

Problem

Transient evidence and replay failures are recorded as **indefinite** waits, so the task is never retried after the dependency recovers.

- A saved replay result that cannot be validated persists `{ reason: "unavailable", until: null }` (`src/repair/loop.ts:2092-2097`, `2129-2134`).
- A fixture-identity lookup that is temporarily unavailable does the same (`src/repair/loop.ts:2171-2176`).
- A failed original replay run does the same (`src/repair/loop.ts:2197-2202`).

`isWaiting` (`src/repair/selection.ts:160-164`) returns `true` for an unset `until`, and intake/refreshes do not clear these waits: `clearWait` is only reached from the review-quota drain, review reconciliation and publication paths. A temporary gateway 503 or transport fault therefore parks the record permanently even after the service is healthy.

## Acceptance

Transient evidence/replay failures persist a bounded wait and are re-attempted after the service recovers; `until: null` remains reserved for explicit human intervention.

## Source-only evidence

Inspected development source at `573d862429ab49eefbfcb99bd1878926024af96d`. The relevant files not changed by the final three-commit delta retain the inspected bytes; the changed review-receipt/normalization code and ledger were rechecked. pullRequestMatches compares the live GitHub view against the saved candidate binding: `view.base === binding.pullRequestBase` (issue48-recovery.ts:225-226), while targetPreconditionHolds compares the same binding against the historical work-record base (:230+). GitHub advances base.sha as the target branch moves, so once development advances the intended recovery is rejected with pull_request_mismatch; repinning the shared value instead breaks the precondition check.

`open()` recomputes `usedBytes` by summing **every** metadata entry with no expiry test (`src/adapters/gateway/store.ts:364-377`), and `put()` rejects against that total (`src/adapters/gateway/store.ts:477-481`). `listByIncident` skips entries belonging to other incidents before loading/purging them (`src/adapters/gateway/store.ts:558-575`), so once the incident that owned the expired bytes is resolved, no consumer reads it again and its bytes are never reclaimed. Expired entries are reclaimed across the store before capacity admission, so expired evidence cannot block new evidence from a different incident.

Problem

The closed-review-wait test runs the whole repair cycle, then requires `record.wait === null` (`tests/repair/loop_test.ts:7531-7537`). Its fixture preserves candidate SHA3 on the task branch and supplies a closed PR7 on a different head ref (`:7457-7510`). Recovery clears the stale wait/intent but preserves the candidate and returns the record to work (`src/repair/loop.ts:1747-1754`). The next work step publishes that existing candidate (`:1869-1893`), creates a replacement PR, and calls `requestReviewFor` (`:3748-3755`), which stores a new bounded `review_pending` wait (`:4260-4275`).

The fixture allows these steps in the same call (`stepLimit: 16`, a 60-minute fake-clock deadline at `tests/repair/loop_test.ts:234-246`). Its fake GitHub port supplies an open source issue when no table is configured (`tests/repair/helpers.ts:302-325`), allocates the replacement above the seeded PR7 (`tests/repair/helpers.ts:533-555`), accepts the review request (`:620-631`), and leaves reviews pending (`:670-682`). Thus a successful recovery legitimately replaces the stale wait with a new one, while the assertion requires all waits to be absent. This is a source/control-flow finding; no suite failure was executed.

## Acceptance

The test asserts the intended recovery result explicitly (stale wait/intent replaced, or the recovery checkpoint inspected) instead of requiring `record.wait === null` after a run that may republish and request review.

Problem

Each telemetry query covers only its own exact window. A request accepted at the end of one window and completed in the next leaves an unmatched accepted event in the first sample and an unmatched terminal in the second, so both samples report `coverage: "incomplete"` (`src/release/port.ts:506-533`) even though the logs are complete and the requests are healthy. Context
The quota-runway feature (PR #135) computes per-model stats exclusively from paid-fallback ledger rows (metered/surplus). Requests served by the Codex subscription path never enter the ledger, so the per-model numbers understate real model usage.

## Gap
- Model-level runtime/quota stats cover only paid spend.
- There is no per-model consumption signal for subscription-capacity runs (capacity history gives bucket-level Codex percentages, not per-model splits).
- Forecasting 'how long can we run model X' can therefore be misleading when the model mostly runs on subscription capacity.

## Proposed
Either (a) add a lightweight per-request accounting row for all routes (model, provider/route, tokens, timestamps — no upstream IDs) and extend the rollup writer to it, or (b) add route-level per-model counters at the gateway admission boundary. Aggregate into the same hourly rollup scheme so the projection can show both the paid balance runway and an 'observability' view.
